packs.name: First things
packs.description: The small set to fetch before anything else: what to have in the house, first aid, safe water, finding your way, the knots worth knowing, the signals that call for help, and which radio channels are for what. Small enough for a phone connection.

packs.name: Home preparedness
packs.description: For a household riding out a power cut, a storm or a longer disruption: official guidance on hazards, a flood plan to fill in, a post-disaster library, medicine, keeping food, making water safe, staying safe around electricity, and radio channels and broadcasts to know.

packs.name: Medicine and first aid
packs.description: Reference for when a doctor is a long way off: first aid and emergency care, children, childbirth, essential medicines and a textbook on how medicines are used, altitude illness, and a medical encyclopedia to look things up in.

packs.name: Food and growing
packs.description: Growing vegetables, composting, and keeping what you grow: canning, preserving, brewing and plain recipes, including ones cooked with no refrigerator.

packs.name: Hills and navigation
packs.description: For walking, camping and the mountains: map and compass, grid references, map symbols, the Countryside Code, weather charts and weather signs, knots, water, altitude, distress signals, and answers from people who spend their time outside. Pair it with a map region from the Maps screen.

packs.name: Weather in Britain
packs.description: Eight Met Office factsheets for reading the sky and the forecast in the UK: clouds, air masses and fronts, how to read a weather chart, the Beaufort scale, the Shipping Forecast, the climate of the British Isles, the local climates of hills and coasts, and weather radar.

packs.name: Coast and sea
packs.description: For small boats and the shore: chart symbols, life saving signals, the Shipping Forecast and when it is broadcast, the Beaufort scale, marine VHF and digital selective calling, ship radio licensing, knots, and the distress frequencies.

packs.name: Radio reference sheets
packs.description: Nine sheets that come with Outpost, so adding them needs no connection: amateur bands for the UK, the US and worldwide, repeaters and data modes, licence-free radio, emergency and calling frequencies, weather and time broadcasts, an operating reference, and the informal preparedness conventions.

packs.name: Amateur radio in the UK
packs.description: For a UK operator or someone working towards a licence: the reference sheets, the Radio Engineering Handbook to learn from, Ofcom's licence conditions and guidance, its rules on electromagnetic field exposure, the UK frequency allocation table, CB and PMR446 rules, the IARU Region 1 band plans and operating guide, the space weather scales, and questions and answers from other operators.

packs.name: Amateur radio in the United States
packs.description: For a US operator or someone studying for a licence: the reference sheets, the Radio Engineering Handbook to learn from, the FCC's amateur and personal radio rules, the national allocation chart, the federal field operations guides for emergency communications, NOAA Weather Radio and the time stations, the IARU Region 2 band plan, and questions and answers from other operators.

packs.name: Learning amateur radio
packs.description: A beginner's course to read from the start: the Radio Engineering Handbook, with the operating reference and the worldwide band sheet beside it. All of it comes with Outpost, so adding it needs no connection.

packs.name: Radio companion guides
packs.description: Book-length guides to 15 particular radios and interfaces, each with its menus explained, ready-made configurations and troubleshooting, and the handbook they lean on for theory. They come with Outpost, so adding them needs no connection. To add only the guide for your own radio, find it under Radio communications.

packs.name: Repair and making
packs.description: Keeping things working: community repair guides, vehicles, bicycles, woodwork, electronics with Arduino, 3D printing, how fasteners are chosen, how engines, pumps and valves work, and working safely off a ladder.

packs.name: Electricity and electronics
packs.description: A course to work through and references to keep beside it: the six volumes of Lessons In Electric Circuits, from Ohm's law to digital logic with experiments to build; the US Department of Energy's handbooks on batteries, motors, generators and transformers and on reading schematics; and the Health and Safety Executive's guidance on working safely with electricity.

packs.name: General reference
packs.description: A compact shelf for looking things up: the most-read Wikipedia articles, a dictionary, a travel guide to the world, and country facts.

packs.name: Schoolroom
packs.description: For learning with no connection: a children's encyclopedia, Wikipedia in simple English, interactive science simulations, a school physics book, and college textbooks in maths, physics, chemistry and biology.

packs.name: Programming without the internet
packs.description: Language and tool documentation, the Linux manual pages, the ArchWiki and freeCodeCamp's courses. All of it together is small.
